subject: Private GPU pool hypotheses, observability asks, and simulation plan
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Sally Quinto <sally@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private GPU pool hypotheses, observability asks, and simulation plan

Hi Sally —

Thanks again for the sync yesterday. Per our conversation I sketched a small set of capacity hypotheses and a minimal observability checklist so we can run an initial simulation and a limited stress run in your staging cluster. Attaching the hypothesis workbook (sim-hypotheses.xlsx) and a short network trace sample we captured from our last lab run (network-trace-sample.pcap).

Top-level hypotheses (please confirm):
- Target sustained throughput: 600 tokens/s per GPU pod under mixed prompt sizes (median 256 tokens, 95th 1024).
- Latency SLO: 95th token latency < 120ms for priority routes; p50 target ~40–60ms.
- Headroom margin: aim for 30% spare GPU cycles to allow short bursts and cache warmups.
- Network: no single NIC saturating >80% sustained; cross-host tail latency contributes <20% of the token latency budget.

Minimal observability we need from your side for the simulation:
- Per-GPU utilization time series (1s granularity preferable)
- NVML-style memory and SM utilization, and queue depth metrics
- NIC tx/rx bytes per host, with p99 transmit latency if available
- Per-host CPU steal/IO wait (to catch network/disk contention)
- KV cache hit rates (if application-level caching present)

Questions / asks:
1) Can we get a 2-hour staging window Tue 6/9 02:00–04:00 UTC for a staged stress run? We’ll run three scenarios (baseline, 2x spike, mixed-tail).
2) Is the staging topology in the link you shared yesterday still accurate? If not, please send the latest topology PDF.
3) Any constraints on running kernel-level perf counters or elevated NIC capturing during the test?

Planned deliverables after the run:
- Simulation report with throughput headroom chart and bottleneck callouts
- Short runbook with mitigation actions (warm pools, NIC tuning, batch sizing)
- Recommended next-capacity size and follow-up test matrix

If this looks good I’ll post a mutual action plan and owner list by EOD.

—
Neha Kapoor
Product Partnerships, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.ai
From: Sally Quinto <sally@acme.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Ops <acme-ops@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 13:05:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool hypotheses, observability asks, and simulation plan

Neha —

Thanks for the clear list. The staging topology is attached (topology-v1.pdf) — note that we have an additional leaf switch between the GPU hosts and the aggregation that we didn’t call out yesterday. Maintenance window on Tue is OK but our on-call rotation prefers tests before 05:00 UTC.

Constraints:
- Kernel perf counters are fine but only for 1-hour captures; extended captures require approval from our security team.
- We can enable a packet capture on the staging NICs but need a sanitized pcap (no customer payload) to be exchanged afterward.
- We do not allow sustained NIC >90% for longer than 10 minutes; if your run pushes that we’ll throttle.

I’ll ask ops to provide the per-host NVML and NIC counters (1s rollup) and upload to the shared drive — should be there by 6/9 00:00 UTC.

Sally
Sally Quinto
Head of Platform Ops, Acme Corp
sally@acme.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Sally Quinto <sally@acme.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 09:20:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool hypotheses, observability asks, and simulation plan

Thanks, Sally — that maintenance window and constraints are workable. A few internal notes and clarifying asks from the run/engineering side: 

Simulation scenarios we will run (short descriptions):
- baseline: realistic arrival process from your prod replay (scaled to staging), single-model, cold cache then 20m warmup
- spike: 2x sustained for 10 minutes followed by return-to-baseline (to validate autoscale and queue shedding)
- mixed-tail: heavy long-generation prompts (95th token length ~1024) mixed with short calls to stress KV cache behavior

Observability probes we will deploy in staging (we will push these configs):
- nvml_exporter at 1s; prometheus exporter for NIC counters; per-request tracing header to measure per-token latency in-app
- an early-warning knob: saturated-nic alert if any interface reaches 85% avg for 2m; we’ll abort the run if the throttles kick in to avoid unsafe states

Concrete asks for the upload from your side:
- CSV of per-host NVML (timestamp, gpu_id, mem_used, sm_util, power) at 1s granularity
- NIC rx/tx and dropped/pkts at 1s granularity; include p99/99.9 latency if you have it
- Topology PDF you sent (thanks) and the expected MTU/MTU per-link notes

I’ll provision a 3-node pilot in our staging infra to generate the traffic and will share the simulation config (k8s job + load generator) in the shared folder. Vanessa — can you capture the runbook draft and add the operator abort checklist?

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai

- Run plan: baseline -> spike -> mixed-tail. Karthik to run traffic, Vanessa to manage runbook and abort checklist.

Deliverables by Thu 2026-06-17:

Next immediate actions:

- Karthik: push simulation config to shared drive and mark the job as READY.

Thanks everyone — I’ll convert these into a brief mutual action plan doc and post the Drive link shortly.
